answer: Retroactive Transaction-Graph Partitioning. After each epoch, cluster all accounts by shared counterparties, timing, and payload patterns; any cluster whose internal echo of identical actions exceeds a threshold is flagged. Enforcement: flagged identities forfeit accumulated rewards and future inclusion. An attacker must build a distinct, believable history per identity—an anchor of real activity and unique edges—before reaching the payout summit, so each fake account costs genuine transaction volume and time, making campaigns scale linearly in real effort rather than in cheap registrations.
